nodes.description: Reported genotypes combine missense variants across the kinase domain with nonsense and frameshift alleles. In transfected HEK293 cells and in mouse oocytes, the variant proteins are expressed at lower levels, bind MEK1 more weakly, or both, and fail to phosphorylate MEK1/2. MOS is a MAP kinase kinase kinase whose expression is essentially restricted to the oocyte, which is why the phenotype is confined to female reproduction.

nodes.description: MOS-ERK signalling thickens the cortical F-actin layer and supports spindle assembly during oocyte maturation, which together position the spindle so the first meiotic division is asymmetric. Mos knockdown, oocyte-specific Erk1/2 deletion, or MEK inhibition of human oocytes reduces cortical F-actin and destabilizes alpha-tubulin, and patient MOS variants fail to restore cortical F-actin after Mos knockdown. The authors propose these cytoskeletal defects as the origin of the large first polar body and of embryo fragmentation; the second link is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated mechanism.
